title: Quasi-compactness and separatedness of spaces descend under fpqc scheme covers
statement: Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to T$ be an $S$-morphism. Let $\{g_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering by schemes [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], and put $f_i:X_i=X\times_TT_i\to T_i$. Quasi-compactness and separatedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces have the scheme-test meanings in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]: quasi-compact means that every affine scheme base change has a quasi-compact source space (one admitting a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme), and separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test. For each property $P$ in the list quasi-compact, separated, separately, if every $f_i$ has $P$, then $f$ has $P$. No representability, finite-type, properness, or Noetherian assumption on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 041L (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact) and 0421 (lemma-descending-property-separated), descent implication, restricted to scheme base and scheme covering members.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary affine test Z → T. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fpqc-finite-affine-test-cover], obtaining A = X ×_T Z, finitely many affine W_j → T_i(j), cartesian scheme tests B_j of the local maps f_i(j), and maps B_j → A jointly surjective on points. This construction has no quasi-compactness hypothesis. Apply the local quasi-compactness hypothesis to each W_j. The definition [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] supplies a quasi-compact scheme atlas of its chosen presheaf pullback. The unique isomorphism from B_j to this pullback transports the atlas; representable etaleness and surjectivity transport by cartesian-square invariance under an isomorphism. Thus [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], points_compactSpace_iff, makes each |B_j| compact.

Each |B_j| → |A| is continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Its image is compact, and the finite union of these images is all of |A|, including when the finite index set is empty. Therefore |A| is compact. Apply points_compactSpace_iff in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] to get a quasi-compact scheme atlas. Project its map to X and Z, use Yoneda fullness to obtain the scheme projection, and transport the atlas along the unique comparison to the chosen presheaf pullback. This proves the defining affine-test condition for f.

For separatedness represent an arbitrary scheme test R → X ×_T X of the relative diagonal by D → R. Its representing square is obtained from the absolute representable diagonal [def-trf-algebraic-space] by pulling back along X ×_T X → X ×_S X. The relative-diagonal square under an arbitrary base change is cartesian, as proved explicitly by compatible-pair lifts. Set R_i = R ×_T T_i. Test the closed diagonal of f_i on R_i. Paste its representing square with the relative-diagonal base-change square, then cancel the original D square. Yoneda reflects the resulting cartesian square, so the scheme map D ×_R R_i → R_i is a closed immersion, invariant under the unique pullback isomorphism.

The R_i → R form an fpqc family by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms], using pullbacks in Over S and the forgetful functor to schemes. Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] to D → R and the closed-immersion hypotheses from the preceding step. Each relative diagonal scheme test is a closed immersion; this proves separatedness independently of quasi-compactness.

proof_origin.place: Tags 041L and 0421; finite affine test refinement followed by finite compact-image union and the atlas criterion, and an explicit cartesian-square proof of relative diagonal descent.

Step 4: fpqc axiom (3) plus scheme closed-immersion descent with no finiteness hypotheses. Edge cases checked: singleton or identity cover, empty Z, infinite index set, inseparable field cover. Duplicate search: lem-a1-space-fpqc-separated-valuative-descent needs the valuative hypothesis too, lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local needs fppf covers, and proper-fpqc concerns properness, so none subsumes the item. None is a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so the citations are acceptable. The five tool_uses are generic infrastructure and are accepted. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem quasiCompact_separated_of_fpqc_scheme_cover {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (T : Over S) (f : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) {I : Type v} (Tᵢ : I → Over S) (g : ∀ i, Tᵢ i ⟶ T) (hg : Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ (Tᵢ i).left) (fun i ↦ (g i).left) ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T.left) : ((∀ i, IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap (pullback.snd f (yoneda.map (g i)))) → IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap f) ∧ ((∀ i, IsSeparatedPresheafMap (pullback.snd f (yoneda.map (g i)))) → IsSeparatedPresheafMap f)
